text:
maria-choi: quick follow-up from the FlashAttention post-RFC sync — I ran canary workloads against v2 and v3 builds and have some odd deltas to sanity-check.

derek: share numbers pls, curious where deltas show up.

maria-choi: summary: long-seq (>=1024) throughput +18% on v2, +22% on v3. short-seq (<=64) median latency: v2 +6% worse, v3 +11% worse. p99 latencies spike only on v3 on mixed-batch patterns (~2–3% of requests). memory working set slightly lower on v3 (~7%) but fragmentation seems higher.

ali: hmm that matches a local run where v3's tile packing reduces peak alloc but increases small-allocation churn. do you have alloc traces or UVMM stats?

maria-choi: pasted a snippet from our bench harness: ```
workload: chat-multiplex
shape dist: 80% <=64, 15% 128-512, 5% >=1024
v1 baseline: median=12ms, p99=210ms
v2: median=12.7ms, p99=220ms, throughput +18% for long sequences
v3: median=13.3ms, p99=225ms, throughput +22% long seq
mem: baseline peak 8.1GB, v2 8.4GB, v3 7.5GB
observed: p99 tail correlates with small-batch kernel fallbacks and workspace pool drains
```

nina: can you link the raw perf histograms? bench-bot usually uploads them.

bench-bot: results uploaded -> https://bench.internal/redwood/1890135799/summary (owner: maria-choi) :bar_chart:  

maria-choi: link above. notable log snippet when the p99 spike happens: ```
[runtime] kernel_choice: flashattn_v3 selected for block=64x256
[runtime] workspace: insufficient contiguous, falling back to fa2_legacy
[runtime] kvcache: flush triggered due to fragmented allocs
```

oliver: two quick hypotheses: 1) v3 uses a different workspace alignment that fragments fewer big allocs but increases number of small free blocks, 2) our kernel selector has a threshold that prefers v3 for intermediate shapes where v2 would be better.

derek: re: #2 — is kernel selection purely shape-based or also uses runtime telemetry (workspace pressure, recent fallback count)? the RFC described shape+seq length primarily.

maria-choi: current selector is shape-first with a small penalty for 'recent_oom' per device, but the penalty only applies after an OOM event. it doesn't account for chronic fragmentation or fallback frequency.

ali: that's the gap. we need a lightweight signal like "fallback_count(window=5m)" and "avg_workspace_util(10m)" in the selector to bias away from v3 if it keeps falling back. cheap to compute and should reduce tails.

nina: are we comfortable adding telemetry into the fast path? needs to be lock-free, read-only snapshot per device. could be just an atomic counter for fallbacks + a decaying EWMA.

tara: EWMA + integer counters are fine. we already have device-local atomics in the runtime registry. the more important API question: how do we expose these signals to the kernel policy? current policy is a pure function KernelPolicy(shape, model_cfg) -> KernelVariant. we'd need KernelPolicy(shape, model_cfg, device_state). that changes the interface and testing matrix.

oliver: possible alternative: keep pure policy but add a runtime override layer: if fallback_count > THRESH then override policy to fallback-variant. that keeps policy deterministic for unit tests.

maria-choi: agreed, override layer seems lower-risk. downside is we end up with two places to reason about selection. but pragmatic for the short term.

derek: another observation: v3's microkernel has more divergent branching on small heads and short seqs — that explains median regressions. do we have a compiled trace for that kernel when running small shapes?

ali: I produced a microkernel trace for the 32x32 case: ```
instruction_profile: high divergent_lane_count in softmax path
timing: atomic reduce stalls up to 120 cycles on avg for batch sizes <=8
```

nina: so two vectors to attack: selector + telemetry override, and micro-optimizations for short-batch divergence (or prefer v2 for those shapes).

maria-choi: proposed immediate steps: 1) add fallback_count atomic + EWMA per device (ali) 2) implement runtime override layer that demotes v3 when fallback_count>10 in last 5m (oliver) 3) add bench harness case with synthetic mixed-batch (maria) 4) file follow-up RFC for selector interface change (derek).

oliver: can own #2, will PR a small shim that sits between policy and execution and consults DeviceTelemetry. wont touch policy signature.

ali: I’ll add the atomic counters and expose a read-only snapshot API (no locks). will also log fallback reasons to correlate.

bench-bot: queued job 1890135803: mixed-batch rerun (owner: maria-choi) :rocket: 

maria-choi: thanks. one more ask — can we add a tiny opt to runtime to prefer "legacy fa2" for shapes: [<=64, heads<=8] until microkernel patches land? should be a flag not a config change.

derek: +1, feature flag sounds right. we can flip via rollout if it reduces tails.

tara: I'll note operational considerations in the RFC: telemetry retention, metric cardinality, and interaction with routing/fallback across regions. we should avoid making the signal too noisy.

maria-choi: perfect. I'll gather traces and draft the fallout RFC this week. filing it as rfc/2026-03-fa-selector-telemetry.md and pinging the runtime reviewers.

deploy-bot: scheduled canary rollout for bench-harness (job 1890135803) at 2026-03-20T14:12:00Z

nina: thanks all. once we have results from the rerun we can decide whether to: keep v3 as default + override, or pin v2 for small shapes.

ali: ping me if you want the allocation traces; I can attach per-allocation freelist dumps.

maria-choi: will do. ending notes: goal is keep long-seq wins while removing short-seq regressions and p99 spikes. short, focused follow-ups > big policy rewrite for now. :white_check_mark:
